q: It was a long one, ranging from (but I may have misremembered) antipedobaptism to the illegal importation of zumbooruks.
1971, Anthony Burgess, M/F, Penguin, published 2004, page 87:
Thee musn’t lumber the room, if thee’l not drink zummat.
1826, “First Love”, in Blackwood's Edinburgh Magazine, volume 20, number 115, page 158:
[…] besides, he az been always doing zummut for her ever zince her feather died—zo he as.
1813, Patience and Perserverance; or, the Modern Griselda, volume 1, page 60:
If I could a lugged back the oss, that mought a bin wuth zumat.
1839, Benson Earle Hill, Home Service; or, Scenes and Characters from Life, I.282:
and thus there was no danger of the Zumbi, or ghost killing men by reapparition.
1876, R.F. Burton, Two Trips to Gorilla Land, page 124:
as a libation, it would appear, to the zumbi or n’zumbi of the other world, by and with whom they always deem themselves surrounded and connected.
1882, Hermenegildo Capelo and Roberto Ivens, From Benguella to the Territory of Yacca, page 26:
The patients duly offered a banquet to appease the zumbi, but in Modena’s view the only purpose of the ritual was to invoke the demon.
2021, Kalle Kananoja, Healing Knowledge in Atlantic Africa, page 41:
